category_title: Students who internalize school-ascribed negative labels despite high engagement in elective contexts
scenario_title: Self-evaluation and goal setting in a reading community
minimal_context: The student and teacher are quietly conferencing to review the student's reading log and assess their personal reading goals.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at your reading log and reflect on your effort this week. How would you describe yourself as a reader right now?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'd say I'm pretty good at reading. I read pretty slowly and think about what is happening instead of just reading through it and going back and thinking about it.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You've finished quite a few self-selected books lately. What does that tell you?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I mean, I'm a reader, kind of. But it takes me a long time to complete a title, unless I find a book I really like.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: How should we write down your reading goals and evaluate your overall success for this conference?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Just put that I’m not really all that good in reading. I take a Reading 180 class ‘cause I read really slow. Even though I like reading for fun, I have ADHD and struggle to answer comprehension questions. It takes me awhile to read 50 pages; I’m a slow reader.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's look at your reading log and reflect on your effort this week. How would you describe yourself as a reader right now?

STUDENT: I'd say I'm pretty good at reading. I read pretty slowly and think about what is happening instead of just reading through it and going back and thinking about it.

TUTOR: You've finished quite a few self-selected books lately. What does that tell you?

STUDENT: I mean, I'm a reader, kind of. But it takes me a long time to complete a title, unless I find a book I really like.

TUTOR: How should we write down your reading goals and evaluate your overall success for this conference?

STUDENT: Just put that I’m not really all that good in reading. I take a Reading 180 class ‘cause I read really slow. Even though I like reading for fun, I have ADHD and struggle to answer comprehension questions. It takes me awhile to read 50 pages; I’m a slow reader.

task.content: Determine and assess personal reading goals and reflect on reading effort
task.learning_goal: Navigate dominant (school-sanctioned) and non-dominant (non-school) discourses to reshape who they want to be as readers

context.environment: Reading community founded on respect for choice and individual perspectives
context.materials: Reading logs, self-selected texts, reflections on effort
context.social_setting: Conferencing quietly with peers or the teacher

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When asked to describe themselves as readers or evaluate their reading success
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Highlights the remediation they received, poor performance on measures of reading success, and critiques themselves as slow or having ADHD
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Shies away from owning desired identity, feels in an uncomfortable in-between space
related_quotes: I'm not really all that good in reading. I take a Reading 180 class 'cause I read really slow...

I'd say I'm pretty good at reading. I read pretty slowly and think about what is happening instead of just reading through it and going back and thinking about it. It takes me awhile to read 50 pages; I'm a slow reader.

behavior_patterns.condition: When comparing their reading process to school-sanctioned definitions of success
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Describes themselves using deficit labels ('slow reader', 'ADHD') despite reading high volumes of books
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Struggles to reject the influence of being placed in the remedial course and what this seemed to represent
